history.summary:
Association football evolved from traditional ball games played in medieval Britain, with its modern rules codified in 1863 by the Football Association in London. The sport expanded rapidly across Europe and South America during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, leading to the creation of FIFA in 1904 and the inaugural FIFA World Cup in 1930.

Over the decades, football transformed into the world's most popular global sport. The modern era has been characterized by massive commercial broadcasting revenues, globalized club ownership, state-of-the-art sports science, tactical innovations such as high-pressing and tiki-taka, and unprecedented professional milestones across both men's and women's competitions by 2026.

key_eras.description: Early international matches, introduction of the Olympic football tournament, and the founding of FIFA and continental bodies.
The post-war resurgence, Brazil's golden age led by Pelé, and tactical shifts like catenaccio and Total Football.
The Bosman ruling transforming player movement, massive television deals, and iconic legends like Maradona, Zidane, and Ronaldo.
The Messi-Ronaldo rivalry era, high-tech VAR officiating, data-driven club management, and expanding global tournament structures.
